title: Vectorised graph data structures
text: graphvec package extends vectors include graph relationships elements, offers tools compute useful summaries graph structure use summarising, filtering, otherwise manipulating graph. Nodes identified position, value: element vector node, repeated values distinct nodes happen share label. Edges stored indices vector, graphvec can represent multigraphs, self-loops isolated nodes without special handling.

title: Vectorised graph data structures
text: node_vec() defines general graph structure nodes can multiple parents children. vector describes graph six nodes. two D elements positions 4 5 different nodes, since node identity comes position rather value, position 5 connected anything. E element position 6 appears edge , remains graph isolated node. node_vec wraps values directly, keeps behaving like whatever wraps. one backed factor, still levels: Subsetting node_vec selects induced subgraph: edges lose endpoint dropped, surviving edges remapped new positions. vectors particularly useful used rectangular tidy data structures, slice way dplyr verbs. Since node identity positional, combining two graphs just disjoint union: node vectors concatenate, second graph’s edges shift keep pointing right nodes.
code: nodes <- node_vec(   x = factor(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "D", "E")),   from = c(1L, 3L),   to = c(2L, 5L) )  nodes #> <node_vec[6]> #> [1] A B C D D E levels(nodes) #> [1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E" nodes[c(2, 3, 5)] #> <node_vec[3]> #> [1] B C D tbl <- dplyr::tibble(nodes, id = 1:6) dplyr::filter(tbl, id %in% c(2, 3, 5)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   nodes       id #>   <N[fct]> <int> #> 1 B            2 #> 2 C            3 #> 3 D            5 g1 <- node_vec(x = c("A", "B"), from = 1L, to = 2L) g2 <- node_vec(x = c("X", "Y"), from = 1L, to = 2L)  c(g1, g2) #> <node_vec[4]> #> [1] A B X Y

title: Vectorised graph data structures
text: transpose node vector edge_vec(), instead vectorised along edges graph. Values nodes can obtained edge vector using $.
code: e <- edge_vec(   from = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 3L),   to = c(2L, 3L, 3L, 1L),   nodes = dplyr::tibble(     id = 1:3,     label = c("A", "B", "C")   ) )  e #> <edge_vec[4]> #> [1] [1:A]->[2:B] [2:B]->[3:C] [1:A]->[3:C] [3:C]->[1:A] e$from$label #> [1] "A" "B" "A" "C" e$to$label #> [1] "B" "C" "C" "A"

title: Vectorised graph data structures
text: agg_vec() third graph type built around common shape data analysis: single parent aggregates elements, e.g. “Total” row set categories. marks aggregate elements <aggregated> instead spelling edge table. agg_df() extends table agg_vec() columns, one row per level (possibly crossed) aggregation structure – e.g. Purpose State columns rows total one dimension, , . nodes()/edges() reorient agg_vec() agg_df() node_vec()/edge_vec() graphs seen : row child another row whenever parent aggregates exactly one column matches every column’s disaggregated value.
code: av <- agg_vec(   x = c(NA, "A", "B"),   aggregated = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE) )  av #> <agg_vec[3]> #> [1] <aggregated> A            B kd <- agg_df(   Purpose = agg_vec(     c(NA, NA, NA, "Business", "Holiday", "Business", "Business", "Holiday", "Holiday"),     c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)   ),   State = agg_vec(     c(NA, "NSW", "VIC", NA, NA, "NSW", "VIC", "NSW", "VIC"),     c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)   ) )  kd #> <agg_df[9]> #> [1] <aggregated>:<aggregated> <aggregated>:NSW          #> [3] <aggregated>:VIC          Business:<aggregated>     #> [5] Holiday :<aggregated>     Business:NSW              #> [7] Business:VIC              Holiday :NSW              #> [9] Holiday :VIC nodes(kd) #> <node_vec[9]> #> [1] <aggregated>:<aggregated> <aggregated>:NSW          #> [3] <aggregated>:VIC          Business:<aggregated>     #> [5] Holiday :<aggregated>     Business:NSW              #> [7] Business:VIC              Holiday :NSW              #> [9] Holiday :VIC edges(kd) #> <edge_vec[12]> #>  [1] [Business:<aggregated>]->[<aggregated>:<aggregated>] #>  [2] [Holiday :<aggregated>]->[<aggregated>:<aggregated>] #>  [3] [Business:NSW]->[<aggregated>:NSW]                   #>  [4] [Business:VIC]->[<aggregated>:VIC]                   #>  [5] [Holiday :NSW]->[<aggregated>:NSW]                   #>  [6] [Holiday :VIC]->[<aggregated>:VIC]                   #>  [7] [<aggregated>:NSW]->[<aggregated>:<aggregated>]      #>  [8] [<aggregated>:VIC]->[<aggregated>:<aggregated>]      #>  [9] [Business:NSW]->[Business:<aggregated>]              #> [10] [Business:VIC]->[Business:<aggregated>]              #> [11] [Holiday :NSW]->[Holiday :<aggregated>]              #> [12] [Holiday :VIC]->[Holiday :<aggregated>]
